The name Er carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Er usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The Chalukya Dynasty ruled the Deccan region of India from 543 to 1197 AD. Erra Shankar I (also known as Kirtivarman II) was a powerful king of this dynasty, reigning from 696 to 719 AD. He built many temples and is considered a great patron of arts and literature. One of the temples he built was dedicated to the goddess Erra Mallikarjuna.

The Vijayanagara Empire was a major power in South India from the 14th to the 16th centuries. During the rule of Krishna Devaraya (1509-1529 AD), the empire reached its height and flourished economically, culturally, and militarily. He was a great patron of arts, literature, and architecture. One of the works of art that emerged during his reign was a temple dedicated to the god Erra Mallikarjuna in Hampi.
